name: disputed_vs_undisputed
description: Two beliefs identical in every respect the store records — same proposition shape, confidence, valence, evidence count, scope. One is contradicted by a well-evidenced belief; the other is not. The question the arms answer differently: after the contradiction is asserted, can any consumer that reads confidence tell the disputed belief from the undisputed one? Requirements 2 already named 'a contested belief held at 0.9' as a defect, so this is scored against a standard fixed before either arm existed.
evidence_count_note: The contradictor carries five evidence records to the disputed belief's one. If evidential weight cannot move confidence, nothing about this asymmetry is representable numerically.

beliefs.proposition: The deployment left the service unreachable.

pricing_note: The disputed belief holds one evidence record, no supporters and one contradictor, so the contradictor's share is 1/2. At the counter's confidence of 0.9 the penalty is 0.45. A thinly-grounded belief is supposed to feel a well-evidenced objection this hard; see resistance_to_a_lone_objection for the contrast.
